CHAPTER V
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 6
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
(2) Forms of physical violence are any acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or cause death.
(3) Forms of sexual violence are sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence are neglect of family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance as appropriate.
(5) Forms of psychological violence are acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of women and children and the best interests of victims.

Article 3
The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women against gender-based violence and the best interests of children that occur in the household or public.

CHAPTER IV
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
(1) The implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of P2TP2A.
(2) P2TP2A in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection in its implementation may establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.
(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands/other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 7
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions. (2) Protection of women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of Sumenep Regency whether carried out in Sumenep or outside Sumenep.
(3) Protection of women and children victims of violence in addition to being provided to residents of Sumenep as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of Sumenep that is carried out within the territory of Sumenep Regency.

Article 8
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics free of charge.
(3) The form of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) The form of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.
(6) The form of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and providing psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

1.8.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the policy’s substantive scope of “bentuk kekerasan” is explicitly limited to four categories: fisik, seksual, ekonomi, dan psikis (Pasal 6 ayat (1)), with definitions in Pasal 1 and elaboration in Pasal 6. There is no mention that human trafficking (perdagangan orang) is treated as a form of violence covered by this regulation. The only appearance of trafficking is in the preambular legal basis (“Mengingat” point 9: UU No. 21 Tahun 2007 tentang Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Perdagangan Orang). Citing a referenced higher-level law does not, by itself, mean the local regulation includes trafficking within its defined indicator scope. The retrieved English candidates contained the same limitation (Article 6 listing only physical/sexual/economic/psychological), so a correct judge should have answered No. The judge over-interpreted a legal reference as substantive inclusion.

3.3.evaluator_rationale: While the policy describes integrated protection mechanisms and service types, none of the provided sentences explicitly mention a reporting/complaints intake mechanism, hotline, or service for receiving reports.

3.3.rationale: Reviewing the original Indonesian text provided, there is no explicit provision establishing a reporting/complaints intake mechanism or hotline (e.g., “pengaduan”, “pelaporan”, “hotline”, “telepon”, “posko pengaduan”, “mekanisme penerimaan laporan”). The regulation sets up P2TP2A (Pasal 4) and describes integrated handling and types of protection services (Pasal 5 and Pasal 8), but it does not state how victims/public can file reports or access a hotline. Pasal 5(4) says the handling mechanism will be further regulated by a Regent Regulation (Peraturan Bupati), but that is not an explicit hotline/reporting mechanism in this text. The judge’s No is consistent with both the retrieved passages and the Indonesian source, so the golden label ‘Yes’ appears incorrect based on the document content shown.
